segments.text: Some of the best moments of my life have happened in labs.
segments.zh: 我人生中一些最美好的时刻是在实验室里度过的。

segments.text: Also, some of the worst.
segments.zh: 也有一些最糟糕的。

segments.text: Like, the time that I took a week to prepare a sample for NMR analysis
segments.zh: 比如有一次，我花了一个星期准备一个用于 NMR 分析的样品，

segments.text: and then a classmate washed out the vials while I was sleeping for the first time in three days
segments.zh: 结果在我三天来第一次睡觉的时候，一个同学把那些样品瓶给洗了，

segments.text: because he couldn't find anything else to use for his experiment.
segments.zh: 因为他找不到别的东西来做他的实验。

segments.text: Interestingly, that resulted in my personal most significant laboratory injury.
segments.zh: 有意思的是，这件事导致了我个人最严重的一次实验室受伤。

segments.text: We all have one.
segments.zh: 我们每个人都有那么一次。

segments.text: I cut my hand while punching a paper towel dispenser in frustration.
segments.zh: 我气得一拳打在擦手纸盒上，把手划破了。

segments.text: No one ever brought it up again.
segments.zh: 之后再也没人提起过这件事。

segments.text: Alright, we're gonna talk about how to avoid injury in the lab
segments.zh: 好，我们来谈谈如何在实验室里避免受伤，

segments.text: and some good techniques for using laboratory equipment correctly.
segments.zh: 以及正确使用实验室设备的一些好技巧。

segments.text: First two lessons already learned, never wash out a vial you aren't familiar with
segments.zh: 前两课已经学到了：永远不要洗你不认识的样品瓶，

segments.text: and don't punch paper towel dispensers.
segments.zh: 也不要拳打擦手纸盒。

segments.text: Let's start with some very basic safety stuff.
segments.zh: 我们先从一些非常基本的安全事项讲起。

segments.text: Your hair.
segments.zh: 你的头发。

segments.text: If your hair is long, it shall always be up in the lab.
segments.zh: 如果你留长发，在实验室里必须一直把头发扎起来。

segments.text: If it is not, it will catch on fire.
segments.zh: 如果不扎，头发会着火的。

segments.text: I've seen it happen.
segments.zh: 我亲眼见过。

segments.text: It could also knock stuff over and include your vision and droop into your flask.
segments.zh: 头发还可能碰倒东西、挡住你的视线，还会垂进你的烧瓶里。

segments.text: Is there anything that might hang off your body in the lab?
segments.zh: 在实验室里，你身上有没有什么东西可能垂下来？

segments.text: Droopy clothing, especially sleeves are total disaster.
segments.zh: 宽松下垂的衣服，尤其是袖子，简直就是灾难。

segments.text: Clothes should cover your body as much as possible.
segments.zh: 衣服应尽可能遮住你的身体。

segments.text: I like to go long sleeve even.
segments.zh: 我甚至喜欢穿长袖。

segments.text: Never, ever, ever, ever, ever wear sandals in a lab.
segments.zh: 永远、永远、永远、永远、永远不要在实验室里穿凉鞋。

segments.text: Long pants, closed-toed shoes and socks.
segments.zh: 长裤、不露脚趾的鞋和袜子。

segments.text: Clothing that covers your entire torso.
segments.zh: 衣服要遮住整个躯干。

segments.text: Always.
segments.zh: 一直如此。

segments.text: I'm sure you look hunky in your muscle shirt
segments.zh: 我相信你穿着紧身背心看起来很健美，

segments.text: and I have nothing against exposed midrips in principle, but not in the lab.
segments.zh: 原则上我也不反对露腰，但在实验室里不行。

segments.text: Of course, your eyes are your most vulnerable organ.
segments.zh: 当然，你的眼睛是你最脆弱的器官。

segments.text: Always wear eye protection.
segments.zh: 一定要佩戴眼部防护。

segments.text: And no, just glasses.
segments.zh: 还有，不，光戴普通眼镜

segments.text: Do not count.
segments.zh: 不算数。

segments.text: And if you feel like your eyes are starting to tingle or hurt,
segments.zh: 如果你觉得眼睛开始刺痛或疼痛，

segments.text: even if you don't know how something might have gotten in there,
segments.zh: 即使你不知道是什么东西可能进去了，

segments.text: use the eye wash because it never hurts to be careful
segments.zh: 也要用洗眼器，因为小心一点总没坏处，

segments.text: and, you know, we've all wondered what it feels like.
segments.zh: 而且，你知道，我们都好奇过那是什么感觉。

segments.text: I've actually never done this, so this will be a new experience for me.
segments.zh: 其实我从来没这么做过，所以这对我来说是一次新体验。

segments.text: It does not feel particularly pleasant.
segments.zh: 感觉不是特别舒服。

segments.text: But it's better than having your eyes burned out.
segments.zh: 但总比眼睛被烧坏要好。

segments.text: Do not eat or drink in the lab.
segments.zh: 不要在实验室里吃东西或喝东西。

segments.text: Despite our best efforts, stuff does sometimes get where we don't want it to be
segments.zh: 尽管我们尽了最大努力，东西有时还是会跑到我们不希望它去的地方，

segments.text: and if it gets in your food or you accidentally pick up the wrong cup,
segments.zh: 如果它进了你的食物，或者你不小心拿错了杯子，

segments.text: that's just a really embarrassing story for your obituary.
segments.zh: 那可就成了你讣告里一个非常尴尬的故事。

segments.text: Also, I would generally suggest avoiding working alone in a lab,
segments.zh: 另外，我一般建议避免独自在实验室工作，

segments.text: especially if you're working with any machinery or hazardous substances,
segments.zh: 尤其是在操作任何机械或危险物质的时候，

segments.text: but it will be up to you and your advisors to make that decision when the time comes.
segments.zh: 不过到时候要由你和你的导师来做这个决定。

segments.text: You may have seen this little symbol before here.
segments.zh: 你以前可能见过这里这个小标志。

segments.text: It's the hazardous materials or hazmat diamond
segments.zh: 它是危险物质标识菱形，也叫 hazmat 菱形，

segments.text: and it's got some useful information in it.
segments.zh: 里面有一些有用的信息。

segments.text: Each little box is ready to zero to four, zero being no big deal
segments.zh: 每个小方格都按零到四分级，零表示没什么大不了，

segments.text: and four being...
segments.zh: 而四表示……

segments.text: Holy monkey, be careful!
segments.zh: 天哪，小心！

segments.text: Blue is for health, the red is for flammability
segments.zh: 蓝色代表健康，红色代表易燃性，

segments.text: and yellow is for chemical reactivity.
segments.zh: 黄色代表化学反应性。

segments.text: A four in health means certain kinds of exposure will kill you.
segments.zh: 健康项为四，意味着某些类型的接触会要你的命。

segments.text: A four in fire is both very flammable and gaseous,
segments.zh: 火灾项为四，表示既非常易燃又是气态的，

segments.text: so impossible to control outside of a closed container
segments.zh: 所以在密闭容器之外根本无法控制；

segments.text: and a four in reactivity means that it is capable of exploding at room temperature.
segments.zh: 反应性为四，意味着它在室温下就可能爆炸。

segments.text: The little area underneath is for any extra information
segments.zh: 下面的小区域用于标注额外信息，

segments.text: like if it's radioactive or reacts violently with water or something.
segments.zh: 比如它是否有放射性，或者会与水剧烈反应之类的。

segments.text: If you ever need to know more about a chemical
segments.zh: 如果你需要进一步了解某种化学品，

segments.text: and what it might do to you or to the world,
segments.zh: 以及它可能对你或对世界造成什么影响，

segments.text: there's the good old MSDS, the Material Safety Data Sheet.
segments.zh: 可以查看老朋友 MSDS，即化学品安全技术说明书。

segments.text: Every chemical has one and it'll tell you all the terrible things that it might do to you.
segments.zh: 每种化学品都有一份，它会告诉你它可能对你造成的所有可怕伤害。

segments.text: If you ever need to find one really fast,
segments.zh: 如果你需要非常快地找到一份，

segments.text: you don't need to go to the cabinet anymore,
segments.zh: 你不必再去柜子里翻了，

segments.text: you can just google MSDS HCL or whatever chemical you think is in the process of killing your friend.
segments.zh: 直接上谷歌搜 MSDS HCL，或者你认为正在要你朋友命的随便什么化学品。

segments.text: There will be information on how best to treat the person who got exposed.
segments.zh: 上面会有如何最好地救治接触者的信息。

segments.text: Of course, you should have always read the MSDS before you even touch a chemical.
segments.zh: 当然，你应该在碰任何化学品之前就已经读过它的 MSDS。

segments.text: Also, you should probably assume that every liquid in a lab that is not water is flammable.
segments.zh: 另外，你大概应该假定实验室里所有不是水的液体都是易燃的。

segments.text: This baby here is a fume hood.
segments.zh: 这里这个宝贝是通风橱。

segments.text: It sucks all the air in there out so you don't have to breathe whatever's going on in there.
segments.zh: 它会把里面的空气全部抽走，这样你就不必吸入里面发生的任何东西。

segments.text: It's also why it's impossible to keep chemistry labs at the proper temperature
segments.zh: 这也是化学实验室不可能保持在合适温度的原因，

segments.text: because the AC units and heating units are constantly pumping in controlled air,
segments.zh: 因为空调和供暖设备一直在泵入调节过的空气，

segments.text: and these are constantly sucking it out.
segments.zh: 而这些通风橱一直在把它抽走。

segments.text: If you're doing some chemistry that might contain some noxious fumes, that goes on in here.
segments.zh: 如果你做的化学实验可能产生有毒烟气，就要在这里面做。

segments.text: And if you want it to work properly, first you've got to turn it on, that's the vent, that's the blower.
segments.zh: 如果你想让它正常工作，首先得打开它，这是通风，这是风机。

segments.text: Now it is sucking air.
segments.zh: 现在它在抽气了。

segments.text: Second thing you want to do is make sure the sash is at the right level.
segments.zh: 第二件要做的事是确保视窗在正确的高度。

segments.text: This has a little thing that tells you where the sash is supposed to go.
segments.zh: 这里有个小东西告诉你视窗应该放在哪里。

segments.text: If you go above that on this model, it'll buzz at you.
segments.zh: 在这个型号上，如果你拉得比那个高，它就会冲你嗡嗡响。

segments.text: If the sash is higher than that, it's not going to properly vent all the stuff to the outside
segments.zh: 如果视窗高于那个位置，它就无法把所有东西正常排到外面，

segments.text: and some of it might get into your face, and that would be bad.
segments.zh: 其中一些可能会扑到你脸上，那就糟了。

segments.text: A note here, if something happens to you in the lab, and if you don't know whether it was serious or minor, you're not sure,
segments.zh: 这里提醒一下，如果你在实验室里出了什么事，而你不知道它是严重还是轻微，你不确定，

segments.text: just tell your instructor, I once inhaled a bit of nitric oxide,
segments.zh: 就告诉你的指导老师。我有一次吸入了一点一氧化氮，

segments.text: which though initially extremely unpleasant seems to subside after a while,
segments.zh: 虽然一开始极其难受，但过一阵似乎就缓解了，

segments.text: but it can have longer term effects.
segments.zh: 但它可能会有更长期的影响。

segments.text: Headache, nausea, disorientation, dizziness, pulmonary edema, death.
segments.zh: 头痛、恶心、意识混乱、头晕、肺水肿、死亡。

segments.text: So I'm glad I fessed up so that I could get taken care of.
segments.zh: 所以我很庆幸自己坦白了，这样我才能得到救治。

segments.text: Speaking of, if you want to know what something smells like, do not stick your face in it.
segments.zh: 说到这个，如果你想知道某样东西闻起来是什么味道，不要把脸凑上去。

segments.text: Waft. Waft it toward your face.
segments.zh: 扇闻。把气味朝你脸的方向扇过来。

segments.text: Also, never test something by tasting it, obviously, and never pipette by mouth.
segments.zh: 另外，显然永远不要通过尝味道来检验东西，也永远不要用嘴移液。

segments.text: I hear people say that, and like, who would?
segments.zh: 我听人这么说过，心想谁会这么干呢？

segments.text: But then I just found out that Heiko, the chemistry consultant for Crash Course,
segments.zh: 但后来我才发现，Crash Course 的化学顾问 Heiko，

segments.text: has twice gotten HCL in his mouth from pipetting by mouth, which I will never forgive you for.
segments.zh: 曾经两次因为用嘴移液而把 HCL 吸进嘴里，这事我永远不会原谅你。

segments.text: That is what these things are for.
segments.zh: 这些东西就是干这个用的。

segments.text: You put that on the end there, and then you go on, you draw the liquid up with this thing.
segments.zh: 你把这个套在那一头，然后用这个东西把液体吸上来。

segments.text: That's what that's for.
segments.zh: 这就是它的用途。

segments.text: Also, these days, most pipetting is done by these guys, which are way cooler anyway.
segments.zh: 另外，如今大多数移液都是用这些家伙完成的，反正它们酷多了。

segments.text: Pipetting is one way to move a substance from one container to another, and it's a pretty good one,
segments.zh: 移液是把物质从一个容器转移到另一个容器的一种方法，而且是相当好的一种，

segments.text: but if you want to pour, you can pour, but let me just give you a tip.
segments.zh: 但如果你想倒，也可以倒，不过让我给你一个小窍门。

segments.text: Commit.
segments.zh: 果断。

segments.text: We tend to get all nervous when pouring stuff in the chemistry lab and go all slow with it,
segments.zh: 我们在化学实验室里倒东西时往往会很紧张，倒得慢吞吞的，

segments.text: but that's terrible.
segments.zh: 但那样非常糟糕。

segments.text: You won't overcome the surface tension, and it'll dribble down the side of the container,
segments.zh: 你克服不了表面张力，液体就会顺着容器外壁往下淌，

segments.text: so just commit at the beginning and at the end.
segments.zh: 所以开头和结尾都要果断。

segments.text: Destroy that surface tension.
segments.zh: 破坏掉那个表面张力。

segments.text: Okay, back to safety.
segments.zh: 好，回到安全上来。

segments.text: The most common lab injuries are cuts and punctures,
segments.zh: 最常见的实验室伤害是割伤和刺伤，

segments.text: and the most common source of those is cleaning up broken glass,
segments.zh: 而其最常见的来源是清理碎玻璃，

segments.text: which you should not do with your hands, but with a broom and a dustpan,
segments.zh: 清理碎玻璃不应该用手，而应该用扫帚和簸箕，

segments.text: and then deposit the results into a bin specifically for sharp stuff.
segments.zh: 然后把它们倒进专门装锐器的垃圾桶。

segments.text: But the worst thing, and it has happened so many times and it is so terrible,
segments.zh: 但最糟糕的情况，已经发生过很多次，而且非常可怕，

segments.text: is forcing a glass rod or a thermometer or a piece of tubing through a stopper,
segments.zh: 就是硬把玻璃棒、温度计或一段管子往塞子里插，

segments.text: and then it breaks, and then right into and through your hand,
segments.zh: 然后它断了，直接扎进并穿透你的手，

segments.text: and you're in the hospital, and you've been paying for the rest of your life, probably.
segments.zh: 你就进了医院，而且你很可能要为此付出一辈子的代价。

segments.text: So when you're doing this, and it is sometimes necessary,
segments.zh: 所以当你做这件事时，有时确实需要这么做，

segments.text: you can use a bit of water or a lubricant or some kind of Vaseline
segments.zh: 你可以用一点水、润滑剂或某种凡士林，

segments.text: to make it easier to go through, and then you hold it close
segments.zh: 让它更容易穿过去，然后靠近塞子握住它，

segments.text: and make sure your hand is not on the other side,
segments.zh: 并确保你的手不在另一侧，

segments.text: so very close and make it go through like that.
segments.zh: 就这样握得很近，让它这样穿过去。

segments.text: Not like this, because that's... no.
segments.zh: 不要像这样，因为那样……不行。

segments.text: When you're done with an experiment, do not just dump the results into the sink
segments.zh: 做完实验后，不要直接把产物倒进水槽，

segments.text: unless this has been explicitly approved by the person in charge of chemical safety.
segments.zh: 除非这已得到化学安全负责人的明确批准。

segments.text: For some chemicals, like common acids or bases,
segments.zh: 对于某些化学品，比如常见的酸或碱，

segments.text: dilution is the solution to pollution.
segments.zh: 稀释就是解决污染的办法。

segments.text: When they get diluted, all that's left is common ions like chloride ions from HCl
segments.zh: 它们被稀释后，剩下的只是常见离子，比如来自 HCl 的氯离子

segments.text: or sodium ions from sodium hydroxide,
segments.zh: 或来自氢氧化钠的钠离子，

segments.text: in addition to some protons or hydroxide ions that are neutralized by buffer ions
segments.zh: 另外还有一些质子或氢氧根离子，它们会被缓冲离子中和，

segments.text: that are present in your sewage system anyway.
segments.zh: 而这些缓冲离子本来就存在于你们的污水系统中。

segments.text: Bottom line is, they can be flushed with lots of water.
segments.zh: 总之，它们可以用大量水冲走。

segments.text: For other chemicals, flushing is not a good idea.
segments.zh: 对于其他化学品，冲进下水道就不是个好主意。

segments.text: That probably won't hurt you, but it might hurt the environment.
segments.zh: 那可能不会伤害你，但可能会伤害环境。

segments.text: Do put the products into an appropriate waste container,
segments.zh: 一定要把产物倒进合适的废液容器里，

segments.text: but not just any waste container.
segments.zh: 但不是随便哪个废液容器都行。

segments.text: Different solvents and reagents have to be disposed of differently,
segments.zh: 不同的溶剂和试剂必须以不同的方式处置，

segments.text: and if you dump some stuff into the wrong container,
segments.zh: 如果你把某些东西倒进了错误的容器，

segments.text: it could totally end up reacting with the other things that have been dumped in there.
segments.zh: 它完全可能与已经倒在里面的其他东西发生反应。

segments.text: Not good.
segments.zh: 那可不好。

segments.text: Rule of thumb, always know the right way to dispose of something
segments.zh: 经验法则：在开始使用某样东西之前，

segments.text: before you even start to use it.
segments.zh: 一定要知道正确的处置方法。

segments.text: This is an apron. It protects you and your clothes just a bit extra
segments.zh: 这是围裙。它能为你和你的衣服多提供一点保护，

segments.text: in case you're working with something hazardous, like concentrated acids.
segments.zh: 以防你在处理某种危险物质，比如浓酸。

segments.text: Aprons are nice because they're easy to get off if you spill something on them.
segments.zh: 围裙的好处是，如果你把东西洒在上面，很容易脱下来。

segments.text: Well, if you're wearing pants, you might hesitate a bit too long before you ditch them.
segments.zh: 而如果你穿的是裤子，你可能会犹豫太久才把它脱掉。

segments.text: Which reminds me, if you spill more than just a bit of anything super bad on your pants,
segments.zh: 这让我想起来，如果你把不止一点点非常糟糕的东西洒在裤子上，

segments.text: modesty goes out the window. Just take them off.
segments.zh: 就别顾什么面子了。直接脱掉。

segments.text: Also, while you're taking them off, you might want to run over to this guy here.
segments.zh: 另外，在脱裤子的同时，你可能还要跑到这家伙这里。

segments.text: His job is to dump a gigantic amount of water on you really fast.
segments.zh: 它的工作就是非常迅速地往你身上浇大量的水。

segments.text: Now, usually, you don't get to see these things in action
segments.zh: 通常你是看不到这些东西实际运作的，

segments.text: unless there's an actual emergency,
segments.zh: 除非真的发生了紧急情况，

segments.text: but to thank you for sticking with us through this somewhat disjointed lecture on safety in the lab,
segments.zh: 但为了感谢你耐心看完这堂有点零散的实验室安全课，

segments.text: I'm going to take this off.
segments.zh: 我要把这个脱掉。

segments.text: Thank you for watching this episode of Crash Course Chemistry.
segments.zh: 感谢收看本期 Crash Course 化学。

segments.text: If you were listening, you learned what to wear in the lab,
segments.zh: 如果你认真听了，你就学到了在实验室里该穿什么、

segments.text: how to dispose of chemicals, how to avoid the most common accident in the laboratory,
segments.zh: 如何处置化学品、如何避免实验室中最常见的事故、

segments.text: how to pour properly, what the hazmat diamond is, what an MSDS is,
segments.zh: 如何正确倾倒、什么是 hazmat 菱形、什么是 MSDS，

segments.text: and how to use a fume hood.
segments.zh: 以及如何使用通风橱。

segments.text: This episode was written by me. Our editor is Blake de Pastino.
segments.zh: 本期由我撰写。我们的编辑是 Blake de Pastino。

segments.text: Our chemistry consultant is Dr. Heiko Langner, who's sitting right there laughing at me.
segments.zh: 我们的化学顾问是 Heiko Langner 博士，他正坐在那边笑我。

segments.text: This episode was filmed at the Environmental BioGeo Chemistry Lab at the University of Montana,
segments.zh: 本期在蒙大拿大学环境生物地球化学实验室拍摄，

segments.text: so thank you to them.
segments.zh: 在此感谢他们。
